White Paper From Process Monitoring To Manufacturing Intelligence: Real-Time Analytics And Predictive Control In Biomanufacturing Source: Samsung Biologics By Jihye Heo, Senior Engineer, and Jinhyoung Lee, Lead Engineer, Digital Twin, Samsung Biologics As biomanufacturing processes become increasingly data-rich, the challenge is no longer collecting information but transforming it into actionable insights that improve process understanding and operational performance. Emerging digital strategies are addressing this challenge by combining multivariate data analysis (MVDA), process analytical technologies such as Raman spectroscopy, predictive modeling, explainable AI, and digital twin frameworks into integrated monitoring and decision-support systems. These approaches enable manufacturers to move beyond retrospective analysis and real-time monitoring toward predictive process management. By leveraging historical and live process data, predictive models can forecast key outcomes such as titer, viability, harvest readiness, and potential process risks. Explainable AI techniques, particularly SHAP-based interpretation, provide transparency into model outputs by identifying the process variables that most influence predictions, helping scientists and engineers connect data-driven insights to underlying biological and operational behavior. The next evolution of these capabilities involves secure data-sharing environments that improve transparency and collaboration among manufacturing stakeholders, as well as hybrid digital twins that combine mechanistic and data-driven models. When integrated with model predictive control (MPC), these systems can simulate future process states, evaluate alternative operating strategies, and recommend optimal actions within validated process boundaries. Together, these technologies represent a practical pathway toward more predictive, transparent, and intelligent biomanufacturing operations while maintaining appropriate human oversight and regulatory compliance. access the White Paper! By Jihye Heo, Senior Engineer, and Jinhyoung Lee, Lead Engineer, Digital Twin, Samsung Biologics
As biomanufacturing processes become increasingly data-rich, the challenge is no longer collecting information but transforming it into actionable insights that improve process understanding and operational performance. Emerging digital strategies are addressing this challenge by combining multivariate data analysis (MVDA), process analytical technologies such as Raman spectroscopy, predictive modeling, explainable AI, and digital twin frameworks into integrated monitoring and decision-support systems.
These approaches enable manufacturers to move beyond retrospective analysis and real-time monitoring toward predictive process management. By leveraging historical and live process data, predictive models can forecast key outcomes such as titer, viability, harvest readiness, and potential process risks. Explainable AI techniques, particularly SHAP-based interpretation, provide transparency into model outputs by identifying the process variables that most influence predictions, helping scientists and engineers connect data-driven insights to underlying biological and operational behavior.
The next evolution of these capabilities involves secure data-sharing environments that improve transparency and collaboration among manufacturing stakeholders, as well as hybrid digital twins that combine mechanistic and data-driven models. When integrated with model predictive control (MPC), these systems can simulate future process states, evaluate alternative operating strategies, and recommend optimal actions within validated process boundaries. Together, these technologies represent a practical pathway toward more predictive, transparent, and intelligent biomanufacturing operations while maintaining appropriate human oversight and regulatory compliance.

Newsletter | June 18, 2026 06.18.26 -- Reduce mAb Aggregates: Practical Strategies Controlling mAb Aggregates In Chromatography Process Development Keeping mAb aggregation under control is a persistent challenge in downstream processing. Explore how chromatography process development choices can significantly influence aggregate removal, and how a more deliberate approach can help deliver higher purity and yield. Keeping mAb Aggregation Low During The Final UF/DF Step Final UF/DF is a key risk point for mAb aggregation. Our new article highlights key process, formulation, and system design considerations to help keep aggregation low during final UF/DF. mAb Aggregate Control On-Demand Webinar Explore key mechanisms driving mAb aggregation and practical strategies to control aggregates during chromatography and ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF) process development. Mild pH Protein A Purification Step With MabSelect™ Mild Elution Resin Protect your most sensitive antibodies, like bsAbs and IgG4, from harsh low‑pH conditions with mild‑elution purification to preserve stability while boosting yield and quality in the capture step. Evaluating Antibody Fragment Purification Using MabSelect™ VH3 Resin In this study, we’ll show you purification results of the single variable domain of heavy chain antibodies from camelid (VHH) and human fragmented antibody (Fab), demonstrating high binding capacities and yields for these targets in the capture step. On Demand Webinar: Design Scalable Downstream Processes With Practical Purification And Analytical Strategies Learn scalable chromatography purification strategies, use advanced tools like SPR and SEC‑MALS to understand interactions and impurities, and see how integrated expertise and knowledge transfer speed development and strengthen long‑term process capability. SOLUTIONS Increase Cell Culture Yield Without Increasing Aggregation The HyClone™ Glycan supplement supports controlled galactosylation in CHO cells while maintaining overall culture performance, with minimal impact on key product quality attributes such as aggregates. By preserving product integrity during cell culture, it helps increase usable yield and provides a stronger foundation for downstream success. • Request Information ON-DEMAND WEBINAR

White Paper Unlocking The Full Potential Of Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs) Source: Cytiva Antibody-drug conjugates are entering a new phase of innovation, with developers pushing beyond traditional design constraints to improve efficacy and expand therapeutic reach. Higher drug-to-antibody ratios promise greater potency, while multispecific formats aim to better address tumor heterogeneity, and novel payloads are opening doors beyond classic cytotoxic mechanisms. Yet these advances come with trade-offs—ranging from increased hydrophobicity and faster clearance to added design complexity and evolving delivery requirements. Progress now depends on balancing scientific ambition with real-world considerations like manufacturability, scalability, regulatory alignment, and commercial feasibility. Understanding how these factors intersect is key to turning next-generation ADC concepts into viable therapies.
